detailed_rationale: Aditya Birla Capital (ABCL) is now a unified operating NBFC-ICC (upper-layer) following completion of the Aditya Birla Finance amalgamation (NCLT-approved March 2025, effective April 2025), plus a diversified life insurance (ABSLI), health insurance, AMC (majority stake in listed ABSL AMC), housing finance and stockbroking/general-insurance-broking franchise. [DATA] Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026): consolidated PAT ~Rs.1,130-1,165cr (+30-31% YoY; screener.in shows Rs.1,165cr/EPS 4.31, the company press release Rs.1,129-1,130cr - minor source variance, both confirm the ~30% YoY beat), revenue Rs.13,459-15,877cr depending on consol-vs-segment cut. FY26 full year: consolidated PAT Rs.3,797cr (+21% YoY), revenue Rs.53,871cr (+14% YoY). Combined NBFC+HFC lending book crossed Rs.2.07 lakh cr (+32% YoY, +9% QoQ); insurance+AMC AUM Rs.5.91 lakh cr (+16% YoY). [DATA] Asset quality is a genuine positive: NBFC gross Stage-2+3 ratio improved 136bps YoY / 38bps QoQ to 2.42%; HFC Stage-2+3 improved 63bps YoY to a clean 0.76% - no slippage or restructuring red flags visible in what's disclosed (company does not break out standalone GNPA/NNPA in the consolidated cut reviewed). [DATA/INFERENCE] Earnings-quality check flags one real issue: per marketsmojo's Q4 analysis, operating margin compressed sharply through FY26 (40.52% in Q1 FY26 to 33.69% in Q4 FY26) on employee costs +21.84% YoY vs revenue +10.19% YoY, and Q4 ROE came in at 10.14% versus the company's own ~13.07% historical average - i.e., part of the headline 30% PAT growth was carried by the effective tax rate normalizing to 25.31% from an elevated 34.92% a year earlier, not by operating leverage. This is a beat-quality caveat, not a red flag on solvency. [DATA] Regulatory/governance items are clean and mostly resolved: CEO Vishakha Mulye's RBI approval for a 5-year term (2022-2027) is in place (COMPLETED, not pending); conversion from NBFC-CIC to NBFC-ICC completed 9-Dec-2025; a new RBI factoring license was granted May-2026 (minor, additive). One item is genuinely PENDING, not completed: the Board approved (not yet executed) a Rs.4,000cr preferential capital raise in May-2026 (Rs.2,880cr from promoter Grasim, Rs.200cr from Suryaja Investment/ABG, Rs.920cr from IFC) - this still requires the usual shareholder/regulatory closing steps; issue price and resulting dilution were not verified in this pass and should be checked before the next update. [DATA] Valuation: P/E ~29.4x (screener) to ~25.7x (marketsmojo, different date), P/B ~3.05x, ROE ~12% (3yr avg 12.2%), CMP ~Rs.391-409 depending on date, 52-week range Rs.243-399/409, market cap ~Rs.1.1-1.12 lakh cr. Profit growth is lumpy at the consolidated level: 3yr CAGR is actually -7% (insurance/AMC embedded-value and one-off swings distort this), while 5yr CAGR is +28% and 10yr +22% - the 3yr figure is a base-effect artifact, not a genuine deceleration, and should not be read at face value.
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for this name, so V1 default is Hold absent a reason to escalate. My own read supports Hold on the merits: the two multi-quarter overhangs from the 2024-25 cycle (ABFL merger completion, CEO RBI reappointment) are now resolved and asset quality is improving, but the stock trades at a rich ~29x P/E / ~3x book for a business whose Q4 ROE (10.14%) is running below its own historical average and whose recent profit beat was partly tax-rate-driven rather than purely operational. That combination argues for Hold-not-Sell (franchise trajectory - lending book +32% YoY, AUM +16% YoY - is genuinely strong) but also Hold-not-conviction-Buy (valuation leaves little room for the margin-recovery story to disappoint). No escalation to Sell is warranted; this is a valuation/quality watch-item, not an asset-quality or governance concern.
summary: Aditya Birla Capital is a fast-scaling, now-unified financial-services conglomerate (NBFC/HFC lending, life and health insurance, AMC) with a clean recent regulatory slate (merger completed, CEO term RBI-approved, NBFC-ICC conversion done) and improving loan-book asset quality, but FY26 profit growth was flattered by a lower effective tax rate even as operating margins and ROE compressed through the year - at ~29x earnings and ~3x book, the stock is priced for flawless execution on a margin-recovery story that has not yet shown up in the numbers.
positive_para: Lending book (NBFC+HFC combined) grew 32% YoY to over Rs.2 lakh crore with disbursements up 28% YoY in Q4, and total insurance+AMC AUM grew 16% YoY to Rs.5.91 lakh crore - genuine multi-engine scale. Asset quality is improving, not deteriorating: NBFC Stage-2+3 ratio down 136bps YoY to 2.42%, HFC down to a clean 0.76%. The overhangs that made this a binary-risk name through 2024-25 are now resolved - the ABFL-into-ABCL merger is NCLT-completed (not pending), the CEO's RBI approval for her 5-year term is in place, and the CIC-to-ICC conversion is done, giving the merged entity a simpler, larger regulatory-capital base and direct market access. The promoter (Grasim/Aditya Birla Group) is participating in the fresh capital raise rather than diluting away from it.
negative_para: Operating margin fell nearly 7 percentage points across FY26 (40.5% to 33.7%) as employee costs (+21.8% YoY) outran revenue growth (+10.2% YoY), and Q4 ROE of 10.14% sits well below the company's own ~13% historical average - the headline 30%+ PAT growth leaned on the effective tax rate normalizing downward rather than on operating leverage, which is a genuine earnings-quality caveat. Valuation is rich by either P/E cut (25.7x-29.4x) or P/B (3.05x) for a business generating a 12% ROE, leaving little cushion if the margin-recovery narrative slips. The Rs.4,000cr preferential capital raise approved in May-2026 is still pending execution - dilution mechanics and issue pricing need verification before the next review. A conglomerate structure (NBFC+life insurance+health insurance+AMC+broking) also makes segment-level asset-quality and combined-ratio scrutiny harder from consolidated disclosures alone.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~29x trailing consolidated earnings (or ~25.7x on an alternate recent-date cut) and ~3x book for a ~12% ROE business, the multiple is pricing in continued high-teens-to-20%+ sustained earnings compounding with margin recovery back toward the ~40% operating-margin, ~13% ROE levels seen earlier in FY26 - a premium that reflects real optionality value in the insurance/AMC franchises layered on top of the NBFC book, but one that assumes the Q4 FY26 margin/ROE compression (33.7% opex margin, 10.14% ROE) reverses rather than persists. Given FY26's headline 21% PAT growth was partly a tax-normalization artifact rather than pure operating leverage, the multiple looks rich-to-fair: it is not obviously in bubble territory given the scale and diversification, but it leaves the stock priced for a margin-recovery outcome that has not yet been demonstrated in the reported numbers - fair-to-rich, not cheap.
